title: fix(types): one caught-fault writer, sendServerFault; four route families' catch-all 5xx withhold the caught error's text
body:
Fixes #23174
Clause-②: yes (widening) — one new export, `sendServerFault`, in `@objectstack/types`

## What changes

`@objectstack/types` gains `sendServerFault(res, status, code, message, thrown, request?)` in `response-envelope.ts`, beside `sendError` and `logServerFault`. It writes `message`, the route's generic text, in the declared nested envelope. It hands `thrown` to `logServerFault` with its stack, as the fault's one log line. It shares `sendError`'s envelope write, now one module-private `writeErrorEnvelope`, but not its log call. The shared builder still has one success write and one error write, so `check:route-envelope`'s `SHARED_BUILDER` pin (2 / 1 / 1) holds unchanged.

The catch-all 5xx arms of the four families call it:

- **`service-storage`** (`storage-routes.ts`): 8 catch-all arms, with `Internal error`. `sendRawByteRouteFailure`'s 500 arm converges onto the writer. It composed `logServerFault` then `sendError` and so logged two lines per fault; it now logs one. Its line still keys by the mounted pattern.
  - `metadata-store.ts`, docblock only: `StorageMetadataStoreError`'s doc said its message reaches the operator "through the REST layer's 500 body and through whatever logs the host keeps". It now says what holds after this PR: on the storage routes the message reaches the operator through the server-fault log, and the caller gets the route's generic text.
- **`service-settings`** (`settings-routes.ts`): the 4 `refuse` tails, each with its existing fallback text.
- **`service-i18n`** (`i18n-service-plugin.ts`): 3 catch-all arms, with `Internal error`.
- **`plugin-sharing`** (`share-link-routes.ts`): the family door's `catch` in `mountFamilyRoute`. A throw that declares no status answers `500 INTERNAL` with the route's `failure` text through the writer, carrying neither its own text nor its own `code` (patch round 2). A throw that declares its own status keeps the envelope it declares, `err.code` included, as before: a coded 4xx refusal, the branded authorization-store outage, an authored 5xx.

Per the direction on the card, authored 5xx copy keeps its text on `sendError`: settings' `SETTINGS_CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE` refusal and the authorization-store outage relays. Every 4xx is untouched. `packages/rest` is not touched; its door stays as it is. There is no fourth copy of the rule: the decision lives in the writer, and each arm only names its generic text.

**One file outside the claim's surface:** `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` gains two `UNRESOLVED_CODE_HELPERS` rows. `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` reads `sendServerFault` and the private `writeErrorEnvelope` as code-stamping helpers whose `code` parameter no in-file caller reduces. Both rows take the `compiler-narrowed` verdict that `sendError` already carries, because the parameter is typed `ErrorCode`. The module is a data ledger that no non-test runtime file imports, so it does not ship in `@objectstack/runtime`'s `dist`.

## Census, multi-line, re-run on `cc14657ed` (this branch's base)

The scanner strips comments and strings. It splits each `sendError(` call's balanced arguments across lines, classifies the status (literal 4xx, literal 5xx, non-literal), and flags a message that reads a caught error's `.message`.

Positive control: `storage-routes.ts` at `3d6392f1fa^`. There the scanner finds the two multi-line raw-byte arms (`invalidToken ? 403 : 500` with `err?.message ?? 'Upload failed'` / `'Download failed'`) that the single-line census missed.

The first dev's census on `920bc12a24` still holds on today's base. Line numbers are at `cc14657ed`:

| family | changed | left, and why |
|---|---|---|
| storage | 8 catch-alls (:979 :1035 :1134 :1290 :1393 :1452 :1491 :1540); `sendRawByteRouteFailure` :246, already withheld, converged | 4 × `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (:1482 :1534 :1552 :1597), authored; 2 branded outage relays (:592 in `authorizeDownload`, :682 in `refuseHeldSession`), ruled unchanged |
| settings | 4 `refuse` tails (:245 :266 :348 :381) | :344 `SETTINGS_CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE`, authored (ruled); :145 `relayAuthzStoreOutage`, branded outage (ruled) |
| i18n | 3 catch-alls (:178 :193 :228) | none |
| share-link | :285, the declared-no-status half | the same call's declared-status half: coded 4xx, branded outage, authored 5xx |

Repo-wide, the scanner also ran over the 10 non-test files that call `sendError(` by that name. No other literal-5xx arm passes caught text. `packages/rest`, which imports `sendError` as `sendEnvelopeError`, is out of scope per the card.

## Levels

- `@objectstack/types`: **minor**, for the new export (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`).
- `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/service-i18n`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`: **patch**. What changes is the message text of a declared 5xx; no published shape changes.
- All five are members of the changeset `fixed` group. `.changeset/23174-nested-fault-writer.md` carries the levels.

## Pins

Each family gets a new `*.server-fault-withheld.test.ts`. An injected fault carries a recognisable, driver-shaped string (a host, a table, a server path). The pin asserts five things:

- the declared `status` and `code`;
- the route's generic text as `error.message`;
- a body that parses (`BaseResponseSchema`, `envelopeViolations`) and carries none of the string;
- exactly one `[5xx]` fault line, carrying the string;
- that line's stack.

Some files pin more:

- **Settings:** the two authored arms are unchanged. The crypto refusal keeps its text verbatim, with its `details`. The branded outage answers `503` on all four routes, with its declared code and message.
- **Share-link:** a coded 4xx keeps its own status, code and message, and the branded outage is relayed on all five routes. On the two token routes, the token appears in no log argument. Since patch round 2, a driver throw (`code: '42P01'`, no status) on both token routes answers `INTERNAL`, a body that parses and carries no `42P01`. A caught registered code with no status still costs one `error` line.
- **Storage:** each raw-byte route logs one line, keyed by the mounted pattern, and the token from the request appears in no log argument.
- **Types** (`server-fault-log.test.ts`): the writer's body, one line with its stack, the pattern key, and a throw with an empty message. A CONTROL case measures the replaced composition, `logServerFault` then `sendError`, at two lines.

## Fixtures re-pinned, because they pinned the text this withholds

- `settings-routes.authz-outage-relay.test.ts` §3: the untyped-tail case asserted `message === 'some unrelated fault'`, the caught text. It now asserts that the body carries none of it.
- `storage-routes.metadata-outage.test.ts` (10 sites) and `chunk-part-record-concurrency.test.ts` (1 site): these asserted a sentence in the 500 BODY. Most sites asserted the metadata store's outage sentence, which ends in `Cause:` plus the engine's own message. One asserted the chunk door's internal-fault sentence. Each site now asserts `Internal error` in the body and the same sentence in the fault line. So each case still tells the outage apart from the other answers, on the side the rule puts it.

## Verification

Every run below was taken on this branch: `d57800f1e` for the tests, `fd5162d10` (final HEAD) for the lint and the gate union.

- **Build:** a `pnpm --filter` build of the four families and their dependency closure (20 projects) → `VERDICT command-exit 0`. `sendServerFault` is present in `packages/types/dist/index.d.ts`.
- **typecheck**, each `EXIT 0`: types, service-i18n, service-settings, plugin-sharing (its test-layer `check:test-typecheck` OK), service-storage (`check:test-typecheck` OK).
- **test**, each `EXIT 0`:

  | package | test files | tests |
  |---|---|---|
  | types | 27 | 759 |
  | service-i18n | 6 | 80 |
  | service-settings | 45 | 823 |
  | plugin-sharing | 44 | 1052 |
  | service-storage | 54 | 939 |

  The final share-link pin edit was re-run with plugin-sharing typecheck: 16/16 pass, `EXIT-tc 0`.
- **Reverse verification.** The four route files were set back to their `cc14657ed` blobs (hashes matched the BASE blobs), the new pins ran, and the files were restored from HEAD. The restore was proven twice: each file's hash equals its HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

  | family | at BASE |
  |---|---|
  | i18n | 6 of 6 failed |
  | settings | 8 failed, 5 passed (the 5 are the authored arms, unchanged as intended) |
  | share-link | 10 failed, 6 passed (the coded 4xx and the 5 outage relays) |
  | storage | 18 of 18 failed |

  At BASE, each raw-byte route's pin failed with `expected [ [ …(2) ], [ …(2) ] ] to have a length of 1 but got 2`. That is the measured two-line shape, now one line.
- **Ablations** of the writer, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Each mutation landed (anchor 1 → 0, blob changed). The types suite resolves the writer from `src`, so no build was involved. Each mutation was restored to its HEAD blob, with `git diff HEAD` empty.
  - A1 (the body ships the thrown text): `writes the declared envelope with the generic text` failed, 1 failed and 28 passed.
  - A2 (the writer routes through `sendError`): `logs ONE line` failed.
  - A3 (the throw is dropped from the log): `logs ONE line, carrying the caught text and its stack` failed.
- **Lint**, a proven narrowing:
  - Population: the `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']` object of `eslint.config.mjs`, minus `NEVER_LINTED`.
  - Count: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 15 changed `.ts` files reports 15 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 ignored.
  - Invariance: `eslint.config.mjs` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

## Gates, on final HEAD `fd5162d10`

The gate list comes from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, with no paths: 68 commands, the same 68 as on `d57800f1e`. Each was run and its exit code recorded before any pipe. The reconcile, `--ran`, reads: `68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, with exit 0.

- **All 68 exit 0** on the final tree.
- **Three needed a re-run on that same HEAD**, because of the tree they first met, not because of this diff:
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET). This worktree had built only the 20-project closure, and both gates read built output for the whole workspace.
  - `check:dts-closure` exited 0 on the first pass and 1 on the second. Between the passes, the first pass's `check:type-check-debt` ran its own closure build, which was killed with 137 under box contention and left six unrelated packages with JS and no declarations.
  - The second pass's `check:type-check-debt` re-measure completed (`26 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number`) and built the workspace. After that, all three exit 0: dts-closure `173/173` across 72 packages, i18n `10 package(s) — all bundles in sync`, dual-build-cjs-loads OK.
- **Two gates this PR made red on the first pass**, both fixed in `fd5162d10` and green on the second:
  - `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`: the two helpers above, now classified.
  - `check:engine-double-contract`: the share-link pin's engine double declared unused `update` and `delete`; it now declares only `find`.
- **Type-check lanes this PR touches:** `packages/runtime` was not type-checked locally as a package, because its dependency closure was not built when that file changed. The ledger module was type-checked on its own (`tsc --strict`, exit 0); it has no imports. CI's Type Check covers the package.
- **At reconcile time, `origin/main` was 8 commits ahead.** None of them touches any of the 16 files here. The tool names two gate-family files as stale on this tree: an adr-anchor JSON and `scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs`.

## Patch round, head `3e9d93173`

One docblock, `packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts`, added to the surface by the seat. Changed files: 17 (+961 / -74 vs `cc14657ed`).

- **Gates for that path:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts` derives 48 commands. All 48 exit 0 on `3e9d93173`, recorded before any pipe. The reconcile, `--ran`, reads `48 derived, 48 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, with exit 0. The workspace was built first under the lock (`turbo run build`: 74/74 tasks, 65 cached), so the gates that read built output measured.
- **`@objectstack/service-storage` typecheck:** `tsc --noEmit` plus the scripts program plus `check:test-typecheck` (0 files / 0 errors) under the lock, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

## Patch round 2, head `3c34255a8`

The contract review FAILED on one item: the share-link catch-all wrote the caught error's own `code` to `error.code`.

### The defect

The undeclared-status branch called `sendServerFault(res, 500, err?.code ?? 'INTERNAL', route.failure, err)`. The engine and driver throws that reach it carry a string `code` and no status, such as `42P01`, `SQLITE_ERROR` or `ECONNREFUSED`. That spelling names the backend and lies outside the closed `ErrorCode` vocabulary. Because `err` is `any`, the parameter type did not refuse it.

### The fix

That branch now passes the literal `'INTERNAL'`. The declared-status `sendError` half keeps `err?.code`: it is the declared limb.

### Why the literal, and not `resolveThrownHttpError(err).code`

Measured from `@objectstack/types` src at this head, with `tsx`:

- **(a) The dispatcher twin.** `errorFromThrown(err, 500)` takes its `error.code` from `resolveThrownHttpError(err, 500).code` and its wire `declaredCode` from `demotedDeclaredCode`. For a plain Error, `42P01`, `SQLITE_ERROR` and `ECONNREFUSED`, the twin answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, with no `declaredCode` on the wire. For a caught registered code with no status, it answers that code: `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` stays `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` stays `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.
- **(b) The record's corollary holds.** `logServerFault({ status: 500, code, error })` logs at `error` for `INTERNAL` and `INTERNAL_ERROR`. It takes the capability-absence `warn` for `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. So the resolver route keeps that path, and only the literal closes it.

The two routes are not tied, so the twin's tie-breaker does not decide:

- The resolver route keeps the quiet path open.
- It would also move a plain Error's answer from `INTERNAL` to `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The existing `share-link-envelope.conformance.test.ts` case for a throwing service asserts `INTERNAL`.

The literal agrees with the twin where it matters: a catalogued code, and no backend spelling on the wire. The `INTERNAL` / `INTERNAL_ERROR` spelling difference between the two mounts predates this PR, on the plain-Error path.

### The ledger row

The `sendServerFault` row in `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` no longer says an unregistered spelling "fails the build". It now says an unregistered literal fails the build, and an `any`-typed value is not checked, so callers pass literals. This is a one-line text change; the verdict stays `compiler-narrowed`.

### Pins

In `share-link-routes.server-fault-withheld.test.ts`, on both token routes:

- A throw with `code: '42P01'` and no status answers `500`, with `error.code === 'INTERNAL'`.
- The body parses under `BaseResponseSchema`.
- `42P01` appears nowhere in the body.

A further case: a caught `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with no status still logs one `[5xx]` `error` line with its stack, and `console.warn` is never called.

### Verification

- **Negative control.** Through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, the `err?.code ?? 'INTERNAL'` pass-through was restored (anchor 1 → 0, blob `4e67298b684b` → `1a99247df9f2`). The pin went red: 3 failed and 16 passed, with `expected '42P01' to be 'INTERNAL'`. The file was restored to its HEAD blob `4e67298b684b`, with `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **The pin file:** 19/19.
- **The plugin-sharing suite:** 44 files, 1055 tests, `EXIT 0`.
- **plugin-sharing typecheck,** with its `check:test-typecheck` OK: `EXIT 0`.
- **Gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` over this round's three paths (`share-link-routes.ts`, its pin file, `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`) derives 57 commands. All 57 exit 0 on `3c34255a8`, each recorded before any pipe. The reconcile, `--ran`, reads `57 derived, 57 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, with exit 0. The workspace was built first under the lock (`turbo run build`: 74/74 tasks), so the dist-reading families measured. Among the 57: `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:error-status-conformance`, and `check:type-check-debt` (`26 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number`). This round's diff: 3 files; the PR is 17 files, +1006 / -74 vs `cc14657ed`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Measured consequence on storage.** Two texts that reached the 500 body now reach the operator's fault line instead. One is `StorageMetadataStoreError`'s outage sentence: its consequence, its fix and a `Cause:` tail carrying the engine's own message. The other is the chunk door's internal-fault sentence about a progress write that matches no row. Both arrived through the catch-all, so the writer withholds them like any caught text. Neither has a consumer that parses it. objectui at `72594f29` greps no hit for either sentence. Its console tests already model the settings 500s with the generic texts this PR sends (`Failed to write namespace`, `Action failed`).
- **The runtime dispatcher's i18n domain**, which serves the same i18n paths and keeps an undeclared 5xx's text legible unless it looks like a leak: filed #23347.
- **Branch base.** The branch sits on `cc14657ed`, which was `main` when the work started. It is not merged with the later commits up to `24e064fc9`, because none of them touches any of the 17 files here. CI's merge-ref run and the queue validate the merged generation.
